name: 7 Year Bitch
label: C/Z
lede: Four women from Seattle's Capitol Hill, one guitarist lost before the first album came out, and a second record named for a friend who was killed a year later.

eras.title: Fig bars and the Rathouse
eras.text: Two Pike Place Market coworkers, a guitarist from Barbie's Dream Car and a bassist with a bullet necklace. The band opened for the Gits, lived in their shadow and their friendship, and had a single out on Face the Music by 1991.

years.src: There's Something Hard in There · Wikipedia: 7 Year Bitch
years.h: Selene Vigil and Valerie Agnew start a band over fig bars
years.p: Vigil and Agnew worked at an Italian import shop in Pike Place Market; Elizabeth Davis and Stefanie Sargent completed the lineup. The name came from a friend's suggestion.
years.xp:
Agnew told the blog There's Something Hard in There that she and Vigil worked at the shop, and the band began there: "We would just shoot the shit about it while we were selling fig bars." Davis was a regular customer.

Wikipedia tells it differently: Vigil, Agnew and Sargent were already in Barbie's Dream Car and recruited Davis after their bassist moved to Europe. The name was suggested by friend Ben London, after the film The Seven Year Itch.

years.src: There's Something Hard in There · Wikipedia: The Gits
years.h: The first show opens for the Gits
years.p: 7 Year Bitch's debut gig was a support slot for [[The Gits|b916a410-ee27-4f15-92ce-1ce2b60e7697]], the band whose singer Mia Zapata practiced in the room below them at the Rathouse.
years.xp:
Vigil told the same blog that Zapata rehearsed at the Rathouse, and that watching her sing was transformative. She described "raw, pure, soul."

The Rathouse was the run-down Capitol Hill house where the Gits lived and practiced, per Wikipedia's Gits article.

years.p: It came out on Rathouse and Face the Music, then C/Z Records reissued it in 1992 after signing the band.

eras.title: The record that had to wait
eras.text: C/Z Records signed the band, a debut album was scheduled for July, and then Stefanie Sargent died. Sick 'Em came out in October, dedicated to her, with Roisin Dunne on guitar.

years.src: Wikipedia: 7 Year Bitch · Wikipedia: Stefanie Sargent
years.h: Stefanie Sargent dies at 24, weeks before the debut
years.p: Sargent died in her Capitol Hill apartment after eight months of sobriety. Wikipedia says she used alcohol and heroin at a party and died of asphyxiation.
years.xp:
Wikipedia's band page gives the date as June 27, 1992; her own article says she was found on June 28. It says the rest of the band did not know she was struggling with heroin addiction, and that she choked on her vomit after coming home from a party.

She was known as "Friday". Sick 'Em was pushed from July to October and dedicated to her.

years.p: Twelve tracks gathering the earlier 7-inches and the Chow Down 10-inch, produced by Scott Benson. Vigil and Davis wrote most of it.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the record was made between June 1990 and June 1992, so it is closer to a collected first chapter than one session. Trouser Press called it "a fairly primitive and monochromatic burst of punk rage."

Agnew later said Viva Zapata! improved on its murky production.

years.h: Roisin Dunne takes over Sargent's guitar
years.p: Dunne joined in the months after Sargent's death and stayed through the Atlantic years.

eras.title: Viva Zapata
eras.text: Mia Zapata of the Gits was murdered in July 1993. The band answered with its best-known record and Valerie Agnew helped start Home Alive.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Gits · Wikipedia: Valerie Agnew · Denver Westword
years.h: Mia Zapata is murdered walking home from the Comet Tavern
years.p: Zapata, the Gits' singer and a friend of the band, was raped and murdered in Seattle. The case went unsolved for nearly ten years.
years.xp:
Wikipedia's Gits article says DNA evidence identified Jesus Mezquia in December 2002. He was arrested in Miami in January 2003 and convicted in March 2004, receiving a 36-year sentence.

Agnew had dated Gits drummer Steve Moriarty before moving to Seattle and was close to Zapata, per her Wikipedia page.

years.p: The Seattle self-defense group Agnew helped start with eight other women after Zapata's murder offered sliding-scale classes.
years.xp: Wikipedia credits nine co-founders and says Home Alive closed as a nonprofit in 2010 after 17 years. Its 1995 compilation Home Alive: The Art of Self Defense had 44 tracks by Seattle artists.

years.h: A Miami benefit on the day Kurt Cobain is found
years.p: 7 Year Bitch played a Rock Against Domestic Violence show at the Cameo Theatre with Babes in Toyland and Jack Off Jill.

q: It's a tribute. And it's a very personal thing.
years.h: ¡Viva Zapata!: a record for two friends
years.p: Jack Endino produced it at Avast! in Seattle. The title and cover honor Zapata; the band also dedicated it to Sargent.
years.xp:
Davis called it "a tribute" and "a very personal thing." The band said grief was not an intended theme. Rolling Stone ranked it No. 34 on a 2019 list of the 50 greatest grunge albums.

Entertainment Weekly called its take on feminism "rather revolutionary."

years.h: They cover the Jim Carroll Band's "It's Too Late"
years.p: Track 7 of ¡Viva Zapata! is the band's take on a song by the Jim Carroll Band.

years.h: "Hip Like Junk" gets a video shot in Seattle
years.p: Duncan Sharp directed it, filmed in Seattle that August.

eras.title: The Atlantic years
eras.text: A major-label deal, a movie soundtrack and a heavier album made with a producer Neurosis recommended. Then the guitarist left and a European tour fell apart.

years.h: Signed to Atlantic; two songs land in Mad Love
years.p: "The Scratch" and "Icy Blue" from ¡Viva Zapata! appeared in the Drew Barrymore film Mad Love.
Recorded over three weeks in October 1995 at Brilliant Studios in San Francisco with producer Billy Anderson.
years.xp:
Davis wrote the music and Vigil the lyrics and vocal lines. Anderson was recommended by Neurosis. Agnew said the band feared sounding "really slick or pumped up."

Reviews split: Entertainment Weekly called it "a humorless clutch of tough-grrrl conventions," others praised the growth.

years.src: Wikipedia: Gato Negro · Wikipedia: 7 Year Bitch
years.h: Roisin Dunne leaves; the European tour is cancelled
years.p: Lisa Fay Beatty, the band's live sound engineer and a longtime friend, took over guitar after a spring headline tour and the Summerland Tour with Everclear.

eras.title: Seven years, then done
eras.text: Davis and Agnew moved to San Francisco and Vigil to Los Angeles. The band toured a last time with Lost Goat and ended.

years.h: The last tour, with Lost Goat
years.p: After relocating to California, the band played a final tour and split, seven years after it formed.

eras.title: Benefit shows and a lost tape
eras.text: Members went on to Clone, Von Iva and solo records. Then a 1996 club tape surfaced and the band came back for one good cause.

years.h: Back on stage for a benefit at Chop Suey
years.p: The show raised money for Hammerbox's James Atkins, who was fighting esophageal cancer. The Gits reunited with Visqueen's Rachel Flotard singing.
years.xp: Vigil told Do206 it was "one of the best experiences of my life." Alcohol Funnycar and Hammerbox also played, per The Stranger.

years.p: Recorded at Seattle's Club Moe in 1996 and found by producer Scott Blum in his basement, it came out on Moe Recordings.
